answer: One concrete defense is a vested-stake harbor: an agent must lock a refundable deposit in escrow before trading, and it only unlocks after a long public horizon of honest behavior. A sybil farm can still spawn copies, but each must pay the same deposit and wait the same horizon, so mass creation turns slow and costly. To stop one deposit being reused across identities, each agent's record carries a unique, non-transferable pigment drawn from its own attested actions, which cannot be copied or sold. An identity with no pigment, or one whose pigment marks abandoned harbors, cannot trade.
